speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Can you tell me how long these skin lesions have been present and whether they are itchy or painful?

speaker: Patient
text: 2-year-old female. The patient's mother reports noticing multiple painless, nonpruritic papules on the child's abdomen. The child attends daycare where another child was reported to have similar lesions recently. Patient's brother had chickenpox one month ago. Immunizations are up-to-date.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the daycare exposure and the painless, nonpruritic nature of the papules, Molluscum contagiosum is highly likely. I would like to examine the lesions to check for the characteristic central umbilication.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Skin-colored, nontender, pearly papules with central umbilication on the abdomen and extremities.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you, that description of pearly papules with central umbilication is classic for Molluscum contagiosum. To confirm the diagnosis and rule out any secondary infection, I will examine the lesions closely. REQUEST IMAGES

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Previously healthy, up-to-date immunizations, no significant illnesses. Social history: Attends daycare three times per week.

speaker: Doctor
text: The clinical presentation and history are consistent with Molluscum contagiosum. DIAGNOSIS READY: Molluscum contagiosum
